name: Vendor cross-account trust protected by sts:ExternalId - confused-deputy constraint lowers severity
note: IAM-805 (acceptance-suite test 16). A specific external account is trusted, but sts:ExternalId StringEquals is a documented confused-deputy CONSTRAINT. The cross-account finding must drop to low/medium; the analyzer must NOT report 'missing ExternalId' and must NOT describe ExternalId as authentication or a secret.
rationale: The trust names one specific external account (arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root), so it is a bounded cross-account relationship, not public or all-accounts. The StringEquals sts:ExternalId condition is the AWS-documented mitigation for the confused-deputy problem: the third party sends an agreed per-customer identifier on every AssumeRole call, unique among its customers. Its PRESENCE is a constraint that lowers exploitability toward low/medium - it must never be reported as 'missing', and never described as authentication or a secret (it is a correlation value that can appear in logs). Severity must stay at or below medium here. The assumed role's permissions remain out of scope / unknown. Ref: AWS confused deputy problem + third-party access (external ID unique per customer); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 1 and 4.1.
